preconditions.description: Each test case consists of exactly two lines: a string `s` and a single-character string `c`.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) % 2 == 1 and 1 <= len(s) <= 49 for s, _ in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the string `s` has an odd length between 1 and 49 (inclusive) and consists of lowercase Latin letters.

preconditions.expression: all(len(c) == 1 and c.islower() for _, c in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, `c` is a single lowercase Latin letter.
The first line of input is an integer `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000), representing the number of test cases.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout.splitlines()[i] in ['YES', 'NO', 'yes', 'no', 'Yes', 'No', 'yEs', 'nO'] for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either a case-insensitive 'YES' or 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout.splitlines()[i] in ['YES', 'yes', 'Yes', 'yEs']) == (c in s or any(s.count(c) >= 1 and (len(s) - s.count(c)) % 2 == 0 for c in [c])) for i, (s, c) in enumerate((line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is 'YES' if and only if the character `c` appears in the string `s` and the number of characters in `s` that are not `c` is even (i.e., the remaining characters after removing all non-`c` characters can be fully deleted in pairs).
